newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish troops clear old mines from Papal venue.
newsitem.headline: Polish troops clear old mines from Papal venue.

text.p: Polish troops have finished clearing mines and other explosives from a former Soviet military airfield where Pope John Paul ll is to celebrate mass on June 2, an army officer said on Saturday.

The mines were discovered earlier this year at the airfield in Legnica, western Poland, where the Pontiff will celebrate mass in front of up to half a million pilgrims during his May 31-June 10 visit to his native country.
Army engineers began a thorough check of the 200-hectare (500 acre) site to remove them.
PAP news agency quoted a duty officer of a local army logistics unit as saying the one-month operation was now complete.
He told the agency that sappers had found 400 training mines and bombs, 100 detonators and some live ammunition, as well as a large World War Two-period bomb.
Moscow's armed forces left various debris and pollution behind when they quit military bases in Poland in the early 1990s after the collapse of communism and the Warsaw Pact.
